name: O-Level Chemistry
constants: Relative atomic masses: H 1, C 12, O 16, Na 23, Mg 24, S 32, Cl 35.5, Ca 40 · Molar volume of gas at r.t.p. = 24 dm³

questions.q: Which method is best for separating ethanol from a mixture of ethanol and water?
questions.x: Ethanol and water are miscible liquids with different boiling points, so they are separated by fractional distillation.

questions.q: In a paper chromatogram, a dye spot moved 3.0 cm from the baseline while the solvent front moved 7.5 cm. What is the Rf value of the dye?
questions.x: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent front = 3.0/7.5 = 0.40. An Rf value is never greater than 1.

questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of ²⁷Al? (proton number of Al = 13)
questions.x: Neutrons = nucleon number − proton number = 27 − 13 = 14.

questions.q: Which pair of particles are isotopes of each other?
questions.x: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. ¹²C and ¹⁴C both have 6 protons, with 6 and 8 neutrons.

questions.q: Which substance has a giant covalent structure?
questions.x: Silicon dioxide is a giant covalent lattice. Sodium chloride is a giant ionic lattice; carbon dioxide and iodine are simple molecular.

questions.q: Why does magnesium oxide have a much higher melting point than sodium chloride?
o: Magnesium oxide has covalent bonds between its atoms.
Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ carry larger charges, so the electrostatic attraction between the ions is stronger.
Magnesium oxide has stronger intermolecular forces.
Magnesium oxide contains a sea of delocalised electrons.
questions.x: Both are giant ionic lattices. The 2+ and 2− ions in MgO attract each other more strongly than Na⁺ and Cl⁻, so more energy is needed to separate them.

questions.q: 10 g of calcium carbonate is heated until it decomposes completely: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. What mass of carbon dioxide is produced?
questions.x: Mr of CaCO₃ = 100, so 10 g is 0.10 mol, giving 0.10 mol CO₂. Mass = 0.10 × 44 = 4.4 g. 5.6 g is the mass of CaO left behind.

questions.q: 2.4 g of magnesium is added to 50 cm³ of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. What volume of hydrogen is produced at r.t.p.?
questions.x: Mg = 2.4/24 = 0.10 mol; HCl = 0.050 × 2.0 = 0.10 mol. Reacting 0.10 mol Mg would need 0.20 mol HCl, so the acid is limiting. H₂ = 0.10/2 = 0.050 mol, which is 0.050 × 24 = 1.2 dm³. Assuming Mg is limiting gives 2.4 dm³.

questions.q: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.x: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

questions.q: Which method gives a pure, dry sample of barium sulfate?
o: Add excess barium carbonate to dilute sulfuric acid, filter, then crystallise the filtrate.
Titrate barium hydroxide with sulfuric acid, then evaporate the solution to dryness.
Mix aqueous barium nitrate with aqueous sodium sulfate, then filter, wash the residue with distilled water and dry it.
Add barium metal to dilute sulfuric acid and crystallise the solution.
questions.x: Barium sulfate is insoluble, so it is made by precipitation and collected as the residue, not crystallised from a filtrate. With barium carbonate, insoluble BaSO₄ coats the solid and stops the reaction.

questions.q: Which of these is an endothermic process?
o: neutralisation of an acid by an alkali
questions.x: Thermal decomposition needs a continuous supply of heat to break bonds, so it is endothermic. The other three release heat.

questions.q: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?
o: It lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
More particles have energy greater than or equal to the activation energy, so effective collisions happen more often.
It increases the total amount of product formed.
It makes the reacting particles larger.
questions.x: Particles move faster and collide more often, and a larger fraction of collisions have enough energy to react. A catalyst, not heating, lowers the activation energy.

questions.q: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What is formed at the cathode?
questions.x: Positive Pb²⁺ ions move to the cathode and gain electrons: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb. Bromine forms at the anode.

questions.q: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What are the products at the anode and at the cathode?
questions.x: At the cathode, H⁺ is discharged in preference to the more reactive Na⁺, giving hydrogen. Because Cl⁻ is concentrated, it is discharged at the anode instead of OH⁻, giving chlorine.

questions.q: How do the halogens change going down Group VII from chlorine to iodine?
o: Their colour becomes darker and their reactivity decreases.
They change from solids to gases.
questions.x: Down Group VII the colour darkens (pale green, red-brown, black), melting points rise, and reactivity falls. Chlorine can displace iodine from iodides.

questions.q: Element Q has proton number 16 and element R has proton number 19. What is the formula of the compound they form, and what type of bonding does it have?
questions.x: Q is sulfur (2.8.6) and forms Q²⁻; R is potassium (2.8.8.1) and forms R⁺. A metal with a non-metal bonds ionically, and two R⁺ balance one Q²⁻, giving R₂Q.

questions.q: Which metal can be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon?
questions.x: Carbon can only reduce oxides of metals below it in the reactivity series, such as iron. Sodium, magnesium and aluminium are more reactive than carbon and are extracted by electrolysis.

questions.q: Metal P reacts with cold water. Metal Q does not react with cold water, but it displaces metal R from an aqueous solution of a salt of R. What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?
questions.x: P reacts with cold water, so it is above Q. Q displaces R, so Q is more reactive than R. The order is P > Q > R.

questions.q: Which test distinguishes ethene from ethane?
o: Ethene turns damp red litmus paper blue.
questions.x: The C=C double bond in ethene undergoes addition with bromine, so the orange-brown solution turns colourless. Ethane is saturated and does not react.

questions.q: Glucose is fermented: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. What is the maximum mass of ethanol that can be made from 18 g of glucose?
questions.x: Mr of glucose = 180, so 18 g is 0.10 mol. This gives 0.20 mol ethanol (Mr 46): 0.20 × 46 = 9.2 g. 8.8 g is the mass of CO₂; 4.6 g forgets the 2 in the equation.
